A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Token Sparse Attention work. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, figures, and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy, attention timings, and ablations in Sections 2–3, plus LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack results in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds scoring and layer-selection ablations, full prefill measurements, and additional baseline comparisons in Appendices A.3–A.6.

M1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same per-head QKV compression, output scattering and residual preservation, dynamic token coverage, and drift-based layer selection. The new scoring and layer-selection variants are experimental ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RULER, InfiniteBench, LongBench, and Needle-in-a-Haystack. The additional experiments reuse existing long-context tasks and input lengths; no new dataset, domain, or task requirement is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds PyramidInfer to the token-eviction comparison in Table 5, evaluates SeerAttention and X-Attention with and without Token Sparse Attention in Table 12, and adds the non-eviction comparator OrthoRank in Table 13. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Added protocols include equal-sized low/mid/high drift layer groups, a layer-selection threshold sweep, and full prefill latency measurements at 8K and 128K on A100 and A6000 GPUs. The new OrthoRank comparison matches prefill speedup because OrthoRank also skips FFN computation, extending evaluation beyond the existing attention-speedup comparisons.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds recent-query scoring versus random-query and query-pooling alternatives, drift-group ablations on both models, and sensitivity to the layer-selection threshold (Tables 7–9). These substantially extend v1's retained drift correlation, token-coverage sweeps, overhead analysis, and dynamic-versus-fixed sparsity study.

E5.justification: Tables 10–11 newly report latency values with ± terms. Their statistical meaning and timing-run counts are unspecified, so additional repetitions cannot be inferred. The existing 200-run random layer-selection experiment remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing result entries in Tables 1–6 are retained, while v2 adds the PyramidInfer row and substantial results in Tables 7–13. Newly reported X-Attention comparisons give 2.72x versus 3.49x attention speedup and 83.39% versus 83.51% accuracy without/with Token Sparse Attention. Table 13 reports OrthoRank at 79.36% versus Token Sparse Attention at 87.02%, both at 1.27x prefill speedup.

T1.justification: The representation-drift definition, normalized drift rank and layer-selection rule in Equations 1–2, and coverage-selection mathematics in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about reversible token selection, compatibility with dense and sparse attention, and improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, including the 3.23x headline speedup. Additional appendix evidence supports these retained contributions.

C2.justification: The new appendices explain recent-query scoring's advantage, justify the 0.5 layer-selection threshold, interpret prefill and decoding costs, and attribute the OrthoRank accuracy gap to scoring and per-head selection differences. These extend the existing interpretation. The original limitations paragraph moves unchanged from A.3 to A.7.

D1.justification: v2 specifies X-Attention settings S=16 and tau=0.9, OrthoRank pruning ratios, A6000 timing hardware, and a 128-token generation setting for the TPOT measurement. Core implementation descriptions and code/checkpoint links are unchanged. The main setup's A100-only statement is not updated to reflect the appendix hardware extension.

R1.justification: v2 adds the OrthoRank citation and a focused architectural comparison distinguishing its hidden-state scoring and shared token set from per-head QKV selection. PyramidInfer, SeerAttention, and X-Attention were already cited in v1. The main related-work discussion otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized baseline descriptions, an Impact Statement, a proceedings footer, renaming A.2 to Additional Benchmarks, and organizing the expanded appendix into new subsections. The main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 7–13 add substantial displays for component ablations, threshold sensitivity, hardware timings, and baseline comparisons. Table 5 gains a PyramidInfer row and revised caption. Figure 7's heatmap layout is cleaned up and its erroneous latency caption is corrected; its results and Figures 1–6 are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps in v1: Tables 7–9 test key design choices, Tables 10–11 establish full prefill benefits while exposing short-context overhead, and Table 13 evaluates a relevant non-eviction competitor using matched prefill speedup. Together these substantially strengthen the method's empirical support and practical relevance. Undefined timing uncertainty and the unrevised A100-only setup statement limit reporting quality, but do not outweigh those gains.
